title: Give each request one object per customer

blocks.text: In the account service, one request reads the same customer in three places: pricing, the address check and the profile update. Each place calls `find(id)` and gets its own copy, so the profile update changes the tier on one copy while pricing goes on using the old tier from another. The database log also shows the same `select` three times per request.

`CustomerSession` is opened for one request and dropped at its end. Write `find(long id)` in `src/main/java/practice/CustomerSession.java`, and any field it needs, so that within one session every caller asking for an id gets the same object, read from the database once, while a session opened for another request gets objects of its own. `load(id)` already reads a row. About six lines in total.
The tests run against H2 in memory through a connection that counts the statements it executes.

cases.says: find returns the customer's row values, and null for an id with no row
two finds of one id in one session return the same object, so an edit made through one is seen through the other
a find for an id the session already holds sends no statement
two sessions get two objects for the same row, and an edit in one doesn't show in the other

origin.section: One Persistence Context Holds One Object per Row

concepts: Within one persistence context a row is one object: find for a held id runs no SQL, a query returns the held object, and another context gets another object.
